title: Huarochirí Manuscript
summary: A Quechua-language text from the Andean province of Huarochirí near Lima recounts the mythical origins of the local gods (huacas) and heroes, drawn from oral tradition and written by an unnamed author. Francisco de Ávila soon translated its first chapters into Spanish. Sources date it c. 1608, with 1598 queried; the volume is held in the Biblioteca Nacional de España.

uncertainty.note: One source gives c. 1608 (Cambridge); a Peruvian journal cites the 1966 edition title with "(¿1598?)". The range 1598-1608 spans both.

as_recorded.value: Narración quechua recogida por Francisco de Ávila (¿1598?)

where.modern_name: Huarochirí Province, Lima Region, Peru (province point; the manuscript is now in Madrid)
where.historical_name: Province of Huarochirí, near Lima, capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru

importance.justification: Principal surviving Quechua-language account of Andean religion and myth.
